switch10k.note: staging build itself does not block reads; the swap is a file rename (122-128ms). The 1.28-1.53s values were measured before the sidebar was virtualized: backend search_notes was at most 145ms and the rest was WebView main-thread work mounting 10,001 rows, not cold FTS. After virtualization search max is 174-184ms.

indexingPipeline.watcherNote: 450ms debounce + about 38ms parse/write; 10k single-file not measured
implementation: Store: yebian.sqlite holds annotations/settings; the index connection opens yebian-index.sqlite and ATTACHes the user DB
IndexService actor writes only the index DB; staging is a full index file
set_vault/reindex close the writer and Store read connection, rename staging over live, reopen and attach user, with yebian-index.old as rollback
startup/watcher/file operations update only changed paths
15-minute full stat reconciliation as a watcher backstop
indexingPipeline.limits: list still returns all NoteMeta rows (10k 0.19-0.32s, 50k 0.92-0.94s); 100k not measured; no background incremental FTS merge; .old rename under antivirus/file locks not stress-tested; sidebar virtualization measured on flat 10k and 50k vaults; 50k index is now 259MiB with contentless FTS; contentful detail=none was only an intermediate experiment

scale50k.method: tools/probe-scale.mjs starts set_vault and polls only get_index_status; after completion it issues one list_notes and five search_notes calls, then inspects the virtualized tree and restores the sample vault
scale50k.corpus: 50,000 copies of sample-vault/shebao.md (4,540B each; 227,000,000 body bytes; 402MB on disk due cluster allocation)
scale50k.switchNote: contentless FTS; four runs after the schema migration, 13.1-15.5s. The older contentful number was 18.0-40.5s.
decisions: contentless + detail=none adopted: FTS drops from ~410MB content + 33MB postings to ~34MB; total index 259MiB
keep the full list payload for now: the tree needs all metadata; 0.92-0.94s after a background switch is accepted; lazy folder loading/compact IPC is the next step if 100k is required
schema migration is a one-time background rebuild: an index without index_meta.fts_schema is rebuilt through staging; the old index stays readable until the swap
staging writes emit a writing status every 500 notes so the UI no longer sits at 50,000/50,000 for the final ~7s
scale50k.limits: identical-body corpus, so FTS dictionary/compression differs from a diverse real vault; 100k not measured; contentless cannot answer phrase queries (current search only uses token AND/OR); the one-time 50k migration cost was not isolated (only the 4-note migration was timed); 50k acceptance used synthetic CDP events
